root_cause.text: nf_tables published newly added basechain and flowtable hook entries with plain `list_splice()` during commit, which made the shared `hook_list` unsafe for concurrent RCU netlink dump traversal while a ruleset update was in progress.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `list_splice(&nft_trans_chain_hooks(trans), &nft_trans_basechain(trans)->hook_list)` and `list_splice(&nft_trans_flowtable_hooks(trans), &nft_trans_flowtable(trans)->hook_list)` with `list_splice_rcu()`, and the commit message explicitly says this is to “ensure netlink dump list traversal via rcu is safe while concurrent ruleset update is going on.”

The problematic behavior was publishing newly added basechain/flowtable hook entries with plain `list_splice()` during commit, making the shared `hook_list` unsafe for concurrent RCU dump traversal. In this commit, the relevant commit path was changed to handle per-update hook lists: `nf_tables_commit()` now calls `nf_tables_chain_notify(&trans->ctx, NFT_MSG_NEWCHAIN, &nft_trans_chain_hooks(trans));` and only then does `list_splice(&nft_trans_chain_hooks(trans), &nft_trans_basechain(trans)->hook_list);`. So the vulnerable construct is absent here, and the fix-style handling is already present.
